notes: de-slop: Check your readiness score. If any domain shows no coverage, run a Bonus Quest on that domain. -> Check your Readiness Score. If any domain shows low coverage, focus your Daily Sprint practice on that domain.

de-slop: Review your readiness score breakdown. Run a Bonus Quest on any domain still below 70%. -> Review your Readiness Score breakdown. Focus your Daily Sprint practice on any domain still below 70%.
de-slop: Book your exam when your readiness score is stable and above 80, with every domain covered. -> Book your exam when your Readiness Score is stable and above 80, with every domain covered.
de-slop: A stable readiness score above 80 and the confidence to schedule the exam. -> A stable Readiness Score above 80 and the confidence to schedule the exam.
de-slop: Your readiness score tracks volume and coverage so you know when you have done enough. -> Your Readiness Score tracks volume and coverage so you know when you have done enough.

de-slop: Book when your readiness score is stable and above 80, and you have covered every domain at least once. -> Book when your Readiness Score is stable and above 80, and you have covered every domain at least once.
de-slop: Complete a Daily Sprint, then optionally a Mock Exam or Bonus Quest -> Complete a Daily Sprint, then optionally a Mock Exam

grammar: 2+ years of hands-on AWS machine learning experience and 1+ year of generative AI implementation. -> Candidates should have 2+ years of hands-on AWS machine learning experience and 1+ year of generative AI implementation.
grammar: Strong Python programming skills. -> You need strong Python programming skills.

grammar: Familiarity with LLM concepts, prompt engineering, and the AWS AI/ML service portfolio (Bedrock, SageMaker, and related services). -> You must have familiarity with LLM concepts, prompt engineering, and the AWS AI/ML service portfolio (Bedrock, SageMaker, and related services).
grammar: Generative AI fundamentals: LLMs and transformers -> Study generative AI fundamentals, including LLMs and transformers.
grammar: Amazon Bedrock: model families and access -> Learn about Amazon Bedrock model families and access.
grammar: AWS AI/ML ecosystem overview -> Review the AWS AI/ML ecosystem overview.
grammar: Responsible AI principles -> Understand responsible AI principles.
grammar: Exam structure and domain mapping -> Analyze the exam structure and domain mapping.

grammar: A clear baseline score per domain and a working Bedrock API call you can reuse all week. -> You will establish a clear baseline score per domain and a working Bedrock API call you can reuse all week.
grammar: Bedrock API: invocation, streaming, response handling -> Learn the Bedrock API, including invocation, streaming, and response handling.
grammar: Model selection: cost, latency, task suitability -> Understand model selection based on cost, latency, and task suitability.
grammar: Prompt techniques: zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought -> Study prompt techniques such as zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought.
grammar: System prompts and message roles -> Master system prompts and message roles.
grammar: Fine-tuning vs RAG vs prompt engineering -> Compare fine-tuning, RAG, and prompt engineering.

grammar: Confidently invoke Bedrock models, compare outputs, and select the right model and prompting strategy for a given task. -> You will confidently invoke Bedrock models, compare outputs, and select the right model and prompting strategy for a given task.
grammar: RAG architecture: retrieve, augment, generate -> Study RAG architecture, including retrieve, augment, and generate phases.
grammar: Embedding models: Titan Embeddings, Cohere -> Learn about embedding models like Titan Embeddings and Cohere.
grammar: Vector stores: OpenSearch Serverless, pgvector -> Understand vector stores such as OpenSearch Serverless and pgvector.
grammar: Knowledge Bases for Bedrock: ingestion, chunking, hybrid search -> Configure Knowledge Bases for Bedrock, including ingestion, chunking, and hybrid search.
grammar: Advanced RAG: query rewriting, reranking, metadata filtering -> Explore advanced RAG techniques like query rewriting, reranking, and metadata filtering.

grammar: Design and implement production-grade RAG systems on AWS with appropriate chunking, embedding, and retrieval strategies. -> You will design and implement production-grade RAG systems on AWS with appropriate chunking, embedding, and retrieval strategies.
grammar: Bedrock Agents: planning, orchestration, action groups -> Learn about Bedrock Agents, including planning, orchestration, and action groups.
grammar: Function calling and tool schemas -> Understand function calling and tool schemas.
grammar: Multi-agent patterns and delegation -> Study multi-agent patterns and delegation.
grammar: Model fine-tuning: SageMaker JumpStart, PEFT (LoRA, QLoRA) -> Explore model fine-tuning using SageMaker JumpStart and PEFT, including LoRA and QLoRA.
grammar: Integration: API Gateway, Lambda, Step Functions, streaming -> Integrate services using API Gateway, Lambda, Step Functions, and streaming.

grammar: Design and deploy production GenAI applications that use agents for tool execution and integrate cleanly with AWS services. -> You will design and deploy production GenAI applications that use agents for tool execution and integrate cleanly with AWS services.
grammar: Bedrock Guardrails: content filters, denied topics, PII redaction -> Configure Bedrock Guardrails, including content filters, denied topics, and PII redaction.
grammar: Prompt injection: direct and indirect, mitigation strategies -> Understand direct and indirect prompt injection and their mitigation strategies.
grammar: Encryption: KMS, VPC endpoints for Bedrock -> Implement encryption using KMS and VPC endpoints for Bedrock.
grammar: Auditing: CloudTrail, Config, compliance frameworks -> Perform auditing using CloudTrail, Config, and compliance frameworks.
grammar: Responsible AI: bias detection, explainability, model cards -> Apply responsible AI practices, including bias detection, explainability, and model cards.

grammar: Secure GenAI applications against prompt injection, data leakage, and adversarial attacks while meeting compliance requirements. -> You will secure GenAI applications against prompt injection, data leakage, and adversarial attacks while meeting compliance requirements.
grammar: Cost management: token usage, prompt compression, model routing -> Manage costs through token usage, prompt compression, and model routing.
grammar: Provisioned throughput: on-demand vs reserved -> Compare provisioned throughput options, including on-demand and reserved.
grammar: Evaluation metrics: ROUGE, BERTScore, groundedness, relevance -> Use evaluation metrics such as ROUGE, BERTScore, groundedness, and relevance.
grammar: A/B testing: comparing models, prompts, and configurations -> Perform A/B testing to compare models, prompts, and configurations.
grammar: Monitoring: CloudWatch metrics, drift detection, quality dashboards -> Monitor systems using CloudWatch metrics, drift detection, and quality dashboards.

grammar: Optimize GenAI workloads for cost and latency, validate output quality, and monitor production systems effectively. -> You will optimize GenAI workloads for cost and latency, validate output quality, and monitor production systems effectively.
grammar: Multi-modal models: vision, image generation -> Work with multi-modal models for vision and image generation.
grammar: MLOps for GenAI: CI/CD, Model Registry, versioning -> Implement MLOps for GenAI, including CI/CD, Model Registry, and versioning.
grammar: Distributed training and inference optimization -> Optimize distributed training and inference.
grammar: Emerging patterns: MCP, agentic workflows -> Explore emerging patterns like MCP and agentic workflows.
grammar: Cross-domain architecture scenarios -> Analyze cross-domain architecture scenarios.
grammar: Consistent above 70% on Mock Exams in Challenger mode with no domain below 60%. -> You should achieve a consistent score above 70% on Mock Exams in Challenger mode with no domain below 60%.
grammar: Your final push. -> This is your final push.
grammar: Full syllabus review across all five domains -> Perform a full syllabus review across all five domains.
grammar: Time management (180 minutes for 75 questions) -> Practice time management for 180 minutes and 75 questions.
grammar: Scenario reasoning under time pressure -> Develop scenario reasoning under time pressure.
grammar: Distractor elimination for professional-level questions -> Apply distractor elimination for professional-level questions.
grammar: A stable Readiness Score above 80 and the confidence to schedule the exam. -> You will achieve a stable Readiness Score above 80 and the confidence to schedule the exam.
grammar: **180 minutes** for 75 questions (65 scored, 10 unscored). -> The exam duration is **180 minutes** for 75 questions (65 scored, 10 unscored).
grammar: **750 out of 1000.** -> The passing score is **750 out of 1000.**
grammar: - **Treating every AI question as a Bedrock question.** -> - **Candidates often treat every AI question as a Bedrock question.**
grammar: - **Not understanding RAG depth.** -> - **Candidates fail by not understanding RAG depth.**
grammar: - **Ignoring AI safety.** -> - **Candidates fail by ignoring AI safety.**
grammar: - **Confusing on-demand and provisioned throughput.** -> - **Candidates fail by confusing on-demand and provisioned throughput.**
grammar: - **Not practicing agent design.** -> - **Candidates fail by not practicing agent design.**
grammar: - **Not practicing under time pressure.** -> - **Candidates fail by not practicing under time pressure.**
